entries.justification: Intended tightening (CR-ADG-01): quoted CTE WITH "orders" AS (SELECT 1 AS id) referenced via unquoted FROM orders/ORDERS. Legacy treated CTE names case-insensitively, omitted the tenant filter, and emitted unquoted ORDERS which Oracle bound to the physical table (leaking all 12 rows across tenants). The AST compiler preserves CTE quoting so Oracle binds to the CTE and returns [1].

Intended tightening: the AST compiler rejects DML writes to the consent-policy column (region) or masked column (email), and rejects case-colliding CTE definitions (WITH "Chain" / "chain") that could cause scope ambiguity across dialects.

Intended tightening (SEC-ADG-16 item 2): rejects comparing an integer literal (tenant_id = 42) against the VARCHAR2 catalog column tenant_id, preventing implicit column-to-number conversion and data-dependent ORA-01722 error side channels.

Intended tightening: the AST DML guard rejects DELETE statements whose WHERE clause consists only of constants, subqueries without target columns, or self-comparison tautologies (1=0, 1<2, 100+200=300, EXISTS(SELECT 1), id IN (id), id BETWEEN id AND id).

Intended fail-closed rejection of unsafe or non-portable SQL constructs: CAST(... AS xml), current_user session probing, subquery in window frame bounds, GROUPS window frames, parameterized current_timestamp(p), OVERLAY(... PLACING ...), and AT TIME ZONE.

Intended tightening (AGGREGATION_ON_MASKED_COLUMN): under TenantConsentMask the AST compiler rejects the masked column email in GROUP BY or an aggregate, because grouping on the raw value discloses its cardinality and frequencies; the legacy rewriter returns the grouped rows.

Intended tightening: rejects WHERE/ORDER BY on masked column email, DML writes to policy column region or masked column email, CTEs shadowing physical tables or colliding in case, uncataloged system table pg_indexes, and quoted function/type names.

Intended fail-closed rejection of unsafe SQL constructs: CAST(status AS xml) (disallowed XML type) and current_user (database session identity disclosure).

Intended tightening (SEC-ADG-16 item 2): rejects comparing an integer literal (tenant_id = 42) against the NVARCHAR catalog column tenant_id, preventing implicit text-to-int conversion and data-dependent conversion error side channels.

Intended fail-closed rejection of unsafe or dialect-foreign SQL constructs on SQLite: CAST(status AS xml), GROUPS window frames, and Databricks-specific CAST(... AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ) which SQLite only tolerated due to permissive type affinity.

legacyDefects.defect: The legacy token-stream rewriter does not iterate a WITH RECURSIVE member: it returns only the anchor rows (8, or 4 under consent) where the recursion yields 24 (12 under consent).
legacyDefects.justification: The AST result is the correct recursive result (3 levels x 8 rows) and every row is tenant-scoped. The gate skips these ids only while the PolicyOracle reports zero violations on the AST path.

legacyDefects.defect: Legacy passes EXISTS through as Oracle's native boolean select item (ODP.NET returns Boolean); the AST emits the portable 1/0 NUMBER form. Same truth value; a typing difference, not a security difference.
legacyDefects.justification: A table-free statement that touches no tenant data; the stakeholder accepts the AST form. Skipped only while the PolicyOracle reports zero violations on the AST path.
